actual_singular: 3.1.66 selects cli → ciṇ before ta in the activity/patient constructions; 6.4.104 removes ta, while i belongs to ciṇ. 7.3.34 blocks radical a-vṛddhi for the two udātta m-final sam inputs. Anudātta nam is outside that prohibition, so anāmi. The two ā-final styai roots acquire yuk under 7.3.33, giving astyāyi.
lexical_maha: 01.0831 is consonant-final short mah; penultimate a before ṇit ciṇ gives amāhi. The distinct adanta curādi at 10.0406 has inherited short mah after ṇic in its history. Its actual ciṇ gives amahi. Long-vowel 01.1042 preserves its original ā and also gives amāhi.
middle_sic: Outside the actual ciṇ 3sg, the three lexical ṇic roots admit the previously pinned ordinary and 6.4.62 ciṇvat paths. Ordinary outer iṭ lets ṇic appear as ay. Under the adopted 6.4.22/lopa policy the ciṇvat iṭ is unavailable to the 6.4.51 loss decision, and remains audible afterwards. For 2pl compare the sound before iṭ using 8.3.78–79. For mah both h and ordinary y allow the two dentalities; in the written ciṇvat branch amahidhvam is additional to the source table.
qualifier: The long curādi ālocana selection gives aśāmi in the pinned row. Separately the Kāśikā under 6.4.93 gives aśami/aśāmi in the mit-ṇic treatment: this excerpt does not identify the specific curādi ālocana sense. The short form remains a contextual source comparison.
separate_actors: With nam, kartari P anaṃsīt and the self-bending object anaṃsta have different constructions. Neither is credited as passive ciṇ. Intransitives receive only their activity third singular.
